author: Inside Edition
description: With zero musical training, Kyle Kilroy is dazzling the nation by performing in his place of work, a waste water treatment plant in Nashua, New Hampshire. He sings everything from opera, to Broadway show tunes to the national anthem. "As I spent more time in the basement," Kilroy tells Inside Edition's Alison Hall, "I realized some pretty good acoustics down here. I might as well take advantage of them."
title: Kyle Kilroy, Aka 'Sewer Singer,' Dazzles Nation With His Voice

author: Inside Edition
description: The Pride flag the Trump administration removed from the Stonewall National Monument in February, will be restored. This comes after a lawsuit, brought by various nonprofit groups against Department of Interior Secretary Doug Burgum and the National Park Service was settled. At the time, the National Park Service said it removed the flag after the Department of the Interior stated that only official agency flags could be displayed on its flagpoles. Inside Edition Digital has more.
title: Pride Flag At Stonewall National Monument Will Be Restored After Lawsuit Settlement

author: Inside Edition
description: Pope Leo continued his trip to Africa, while the White House continued its war of words with the leader of the Catholic Church after criticism of the Iran War. When asked about the Pope's comments, Vice President JD Vance, a converted Catholic himself, told Fox News' Bret Baier, "I certainly think that in some cases, it would be best for the Vatican to stick to matters of morality. To stick to matters of what’s going on in the Catholic Church." Inside Edition Digital’s Mara Montalbano has more.
title: Vice President Vance Says Pope Should 'Stick To Matters Of Morality'

author: Inside Edition
description: The person who was caught on camera hanging on a pipe inside that burst inside the George Mason University Parking Garage in the now viral video is speaking out about what happened to Inside Edition Digital and says "accountability that needs to be taken. So, when it initially happened, heart dropped. It wasn't intentional." Fawaz Odunbaku, 21, an emcee from Texas was in the Washington DC metro area working at a conference when a night of fun would become something that would be shared all over social media and across the country. Odunbaku has since apologized and has agreed to pay the damages.
title: Man Doing Pull Ups On Pipe That Burst in Viral Clip Takes Responsibility
